headline: A hidden character sitting in the note editor's file made our code search tool skip that entire file without saying so. It is gone now, and the tool sees the file.
matters: The note editor is the biggest and busiest screen in the app, the one where you place and drag notes. Every time anyone searched the app's code looking for a problem, that screen was silently left out and the search still reported back clean. So some past clean answers had never actually looked there. I reran the main one and it is still clean, meaning nothing was in fact hiding, but the answer is now trustworthy rather than lucky. Nothing about how the app looks or behaves changed.
detail: src/components/PianoRoll.tsx held the only NUL byte in any source file in the tree, at offset 32584, inside the sentinel MIXED_VOICE. grep classifies a file containing NUL as binary and skips it: grep -c MIXED_VOICE exited 1 with no output where grep -ac returned 7. Fix spells the sentinel as the escape \0mixed instead of a raw byte, so the runtime string is unchanged (\0mixed === String.fromCharCode(0)+'mixed' is true, length 6, codepoint 0) and it still cannot collide with a real voice id. Re-ran the sweep that produced audit finding F15: 11 localStorage hits, none in PianoRoll.tsx, so F15's conclusion holds. Also re-checked the gesture-reachability sweep against this file: openRegionIdRef at line 219 is a correct guard on async fetch continuations across a region switch, not a defect. Confirmed still present and NOT fixed here, booked under README-7: the stale 'Draw Mode (F6)' comment at line 118 where the binding is B. Merged tree lanes all green, exit codes read directly: cargo 264 passed 0 failed, npm run build clean with zero warnings, vitest 352 passed across 33 files, no src/bindings.ts drift.

headline: The app was offering a sixth FM instrument channel that the S3K sound driver does not actually have. New songs now get five, which is the real number.
matters: On the Genesis, the sixth FM voice and the drum channel are the same piece of hardware. The app was listing both at once, so it offered seven voices on a chip that has six. Anyone writing a song could put music on a channel that would not exist once it reached the game. New songs now show the five FM channels that are really there, plus drums. Your own ruling that the driver decides this, not the song, is what this implements. Nothing you have already written is deleted or broken: an existing song that used that sixth channel keeps it and still opens.
detail: FlamedriverProfile::channel_layout() listed six FmChannelInfo entries including index 5 named 'FM6/DAC' plus a separate dac_channels entry, so 6+1=7 voices (audit F31). Corrected to five FM voices; channel 6 stays declared once as the DAC. Derived from driver source per the derived-never-copied bar, not from the audit note: skdisasm/Sound/Z80 Sound Driver.asm line 1907 reads 'FM6 music track (does not exist in this driver)', lines 177-182 lay zSongFM6_DAC out ahead of FM1..FM5 as one shared slot, and line 2252 computes the driver's own number of FM tracks as (zSongPSG1-zSongFM1)/zTrack.len = 5. Implements the first work owner ruling d-7 ('driver-decides', settled 2026-08-24) implies. Migration checked rather than assumed: default_lane_name already returns Option and documents None for a channel absent from the layout, and ChannelAssignment::Fm(n) is never validated against the layout, so an existing Fm(5) track is neither deleted nor crashed; what changes is the roster offered to new projects and in AddTrackDialog. Added the missing invariant guard (FM voices + DAC channels <= 6) naming the mismatch in its failure, poisoned red-first by reintroducing the defect: fires with 'advertises 6 FM voices plus 1 DAC channels = 7'. Guard scope is stated in its own doc comment as covering only the profiles it registers, since lib.rs has no shared registry constructor to borrow. STILL OPEN and not touched here: an existing FM6 track still exports, which is F30's double-header defect and F27's playback question.

headline: Saving a song as a VGM file silently threw away every drum and still reported success. It now warns you by name which drum tracks were left out.
matters: You could have exported a song, been told it worked, and got a file with no percussion in it with nothing to suggest anything was missing. That is now impossible: the export names the drum tracks it could not include. It does not yet include them, and that is a real decision I need from you rather than something I should just spend days on, so it is written up as its own question. The short version is that nothing can currently produce a VGM at all, because that button was never connected, so the gap costs you nothing today and my recommendation is to do the drum work at the moment the button gets wired rather than now.
detail: F29. export_vgm_data hit ChannelAssignment::Dac(_) => continue and dropped every DAC track before reading a note; export_vgm returned a bare byte count. Now returns VgmExport { data, skipped_dac_tracks }; the command appends a warning naming them. Three tests poisoned red-first: reinstating the bare continue fires an_audible_dac_track_is_reported_as_skipped with left [] right ['Kick']. Two are controls the poison deliberately does not kill, guarding the inverse defect (unconditional population) and the empty-DAC-lane case every new project gets from the roster. Real DAC export needs a 0x67 PCM data block plus 0x8n write-and-wait interleaved sample-accurately with FM and PSG events, so the tick-based event loop must become sample-accurate: booked size corrected from M to L and parked as decision d-10. Dead UI path verified firsthand: exportVgm is in bindings.ts and api/ipc.ts, no component calls it. Merged fd6d21b. Merged-tree lanes: cargo 268 passed 0 failed, build exit 0 zero warnings, vitest 352/352 across 33 files, no bindings drift.

headline: The export that actually reaches your game was shipping songs with no drum samples at all, and calling it a success. It now carries them.
matters: This is the one that mattered most today. When you exported a song to take into the game, the drum sounds were never copied out. The app looked for them in the wrong place, found nothing, and said nothing, so the export reported success and the drums were simply gone. Anything you exported before now needs exporting again if it had drums. It is fixed, and more importantly it can no longer fail quietly: if a drum sound is missing the export now stops and tells you exactly which file it wanted and where, and if you have not saved the project yet it tells you to save first, because it cannot find the sounds until you do.
detail: F33. DacInstrument::pcm_file is a bare filename (commands.rs writes format!('{id}.pcm')) that every other consumer resolves as <project>/instruments/dac/<pcm_file>, but export/smps.rs did Path::new(&inst.pcm_file), resolving against the process CWD where it essentially never exists, then guarded the copy on a bare .exists() with no else branch. Same silent-drop class as F29, on the path that reaches the game rather than the one nothing can call. Threaded the project dir through: DriverProfile::export_song and smps::write_export take project_dir Option<&Path>, read from ProjectManager::project_path at the single call site; no IPC signature changed so bindings.ts is untouched. All four silent skips in the block became reported failures; the two defensive ones (no instrument, not in bank) are already caught upstream by validate_for_export, which was checked rather than assumed. No test had ever exercised this path, which is why a green suite never caught it: added three, poisoned red-first. Restoring Path::new fails the_dac_sample_is_copied_into_the_export with the sample expected at a bare filename and no directory, which is the CWD lookup made visible. Merged c47a938. Merged-tree lanes: cargo 271 passed 0 failed, build exit 0 zero warnings, vitest 352/352 across 33 files, no bindings drift.

headline: Two tests that check importing music out of a real game cartridge could not actually fail. Both can now, and one of them was never checking anything at all.
matters: These two are your safety net for reading music out of commercial Genesis games. The first problem was that they looked for the cartridge file at a fixed location on this machine, and if it was not there they quietly declared success, so on any other computer they would report all clear having looked at nothing. The second problem is the one I did not expect: one of them imported nineteen songs, printed the word ERROR next to any that failed, and then passed regardless. Every single import could have failed and it would still have said fine. Both now fail properly, and I checked they do by deliberately breaking them three different ways.
detail: F32, two defects rather than the booked one. First: both Zyrinx tests hardcoded an absolute path under /home/volence and returned early when absent, printing a note cargo captures, so on any other tree they passed having checked nothing. Path now from SERAPH_ZYRINX_ROM defaulting to the same location; a missing ROM panics with instructions; skipping requires SERAPH_SKIP_ROM_TESTS set deliberately. Second, unbooked: test_import_all_zyrinx_songs looped 19 imports, eprintln'd ERROR on failure, and asserted nothing, so it could not fail. Now collects failures and zero-note imports and gates on both. Gate values measured not transcribed: all 19 slots import with 0 errors and 0 warnings, note counts 5,702..571,753; assertions encode the invariants (every slot imports, an imported song has notes) rather than a snapshot. Poisoned three ways: a missing ROM fails both tests where they used to pass; the opt-out skips without failing with its notice recoverable under --nocapture; widening the slot range fails the batch test naming six bad slots where it previously printed and passed. Slot 0 deliberately left out of the range despite the driver reporting valid IDs 0-19: it imports as 'Silence' with 6,868 notes, byte for byte slot 1 Main Title's count, suggesting slot 0 resolves to slot 1's data. Gating on unverified behaviour would ratify it, so booked as F35. Merged b8bc434. Merged-tree lanes: cargo 271 passed 0 failed, build exit 0 zero warnings, vitest 352/352, no bindings drift.

headline: Twenty three instruments in your Batman library were named after a song that does not exist. They are Main Title's, and they now say so.
matters: The Batman cartridge lists twenty songs, but the first one is not a song at all: it is the command that stops the music. It points at the same data as Main Title, so the app read it as a real song called Silence, and because it read it first, every instrument it found there got named after it. Twenty three of the two hundred and twelve instruments you can browse were labelled Silence voice something, when they are Main Title's instruments. They have been renamed. Nothing about how any of them sounds has changed, and I proved that before touching the files: every sound setting is identical, only the labels moved. Asking the app to import Silence now tells you it is not a song instead of quietly handing you Main Title.
detail: F35. SONG_INDEX[0] and SONG_INDEX[1] are both (0,0), the table's only duplicate; 20 slots map to 19 distinct songs with every bank contiguous and none unmapped, so slot 0 is the silence/stop command pointed at valid data. library::extract iterated from 0, so slot 0 was seen first and won the naming: 23 of 212 entries shipped as 'Silence voice NN', filenames included, provenance ['Silence','Main Title',...]. Verified by running the extraction, not by reading code. Code fix: parse_zyrinx_song refuses slot 0 naming what it is and which song it aliases; extract_zyrinx iterates 1.. so stats read songs=19 not 20. Data fix: re-extracted the library, proven a pure relabelling before applying (hash sets identical 212=212; the only differing instrument field across all 212 is name; zero sound parameters changed), safe because the library carries no curation (measured 0 tagged, 0 hand-renamed). Re-running extraction on the applied tree changes nothing further. Three guards needing no ROM since the refusal precedes ROM access, so unlike F32's they run on every tree; poisoned red-first, removing the guard makes slot 0 fall through to 'ROM too short for bank 1 header', the same error a real song gives. One control proves the refusal is specific to slot 0; one asserts the index table's shape so a future remap fails loudly. Merged 7753832. Merged-tree lanes: cargo 274 passed 0 failed, build exit 0 zero warnings, vitest 352/352, no bindings drift.

headline: Tidied up so the safety check added earlier today cannot miss a driver that gets added later.
matters: Small and preventative, no visible change. Earlier today I added a check that stops the app from claiming the sound chip has more voices than it does. That check could only see a list written out by hand, so when your own engine's sound driver gets added it would have slipped past unchecked while everything still looked fine. There is now one place where drivers are registered, and the check reads from it, so anything added there is checked automatically.
detail: F34, the follow-up F31 booked rather than widening its own scope. The registry was constructed inline at three sites (lib.rs, the overlap audio harness, a manager test helper), each re-typing the same registration, so F31's FM+DAC<=6 guard could only cover the list its own test re-typed. Adds driver::default_registry() as the single registration site, used at all three, plus DriverRegistry::profiles() so the invariant asserts over what the app actually registers. Poisoned two ways since 'covers every driver' and 'can still catch one' are different claims: emptying the registry fails on the guard's explicit emptiness control rather than passing vacuously, and re-adding FM6 to Flamedriver still fires the invariant, now reached through the registry. Removed four imports this made unused; the remaining unused-variable warning in smps_mapper.rs is pre-existing and untouched. Merged 72391ef. Merged-tree lanes: cargo 274 passed 0 failed, build exit 0 zero warnings, vitest 352/352, no bindings drift.

headline: Exporting a WAV always gave you exactly sixty seconds, whatever the song's real length. It now exports the whole song.
matters: Any song longer than a minute was being cut off at sixty seconds when you exported audio, and anything shorter was padded out with silence to fill the minute. Nothing said so. The export now runs to the actual end of your song, with two seconds on the end so the last notes ring out instead of being chopped. Also in this batch: the library extraction tool's help text could never be shown, because it demanded an output folder before it would even tell you what it wanted; the app advertised an export format called binary that was never built; and a comment claimed a key that was not the key.
detail: README pass items 1, 3, 5, 7. Item 3 is the significant one: TopBar called ipc.exportWav(path, 60), so every WAV was exactly 60s. Added ProjectManager::song_duration_seconds() measured from region AND note extents (a note may run past its region's declared duration) plus a 2s release tail; export_wav's duration is now Option<f64>, None meaning whole song, UI passes None, bindings.ts regenerated and committed. Expectation derived not transcribed: 120bpm/480tpb means 1920 ticks = 4 beats = 2.0s, +2.0s tail = 4.0s; second test is a control proving duration tracks the song rather than being another constant. Item 1: get('out') was hoisted above the subcommand match so --help and any unknown subcommand died on 'missing --out' and usage() was unreachable; resolved per-arm, verified --help prints and a real command still reports a genuinely missing --out. Item 5: export_formats advertised 'binary' with no implementation; withdrawn (the method has no callers at all, which is why the false claim never failed anything). Item 7: 'Draw Mode (F6)' reworded since F6 is an audit item number and the binding is B. NOT fixed, reclassified with evidence: item 6 is not a defect, the S3K driver genuinely implements FM3 special mode (Z80 Sound Driver.asm:818 branches on it, with zGetSpecialFM3DataPointer and zSpecialFreqCommands), so supports_feature is truthful and the gap is that Seraph offers no way to author it; item 8, get_channel_overlaps, is correct backend code with no UI surface, and choosing where warnings appear is a design call not a defect fix. Merged e899992. Lanes: cargo 276 passed 0 failed, build exit 0 zero warnings, vitest 352/352.

headline: The intermittent test failure that has been unidentified for weeks is found and fixed. It was the test giving up, not the app misbehaving.
matters: One test in the suite failed roughly once every six full runs and nobody had ever caught its name, so it could not be fixed. It surfaced today and I captured the whole log this time. Nothing was wrong with the app: the test waited up to one second for something to happen, and when the machine was busy running everything at once, one second was occasionally not enough, so it declared failure. It now waits for the work to actually finish instead of watching a clock, so load cannot affect it. This matters because an unpredictable failure trains you to ignore red, and then a real one goes unnoticed.
detail: FLAKE identified as ArrangementView.test.tsx 'Ctrl+C then Ctrl+V pastes at the bar-snapped seek cursor'. Not a race: three waitFor calls, the first spending its full 1000ms default budget under loaded full-suite runs and reporting 'Number of calls: 0', which reads as the paste never happening rather than the assertion giving up; the failing run's 1030ms duration is the tell. Diagnosis proven, after a first attempt that was invalid (a double-comma edit produced a syntax error and 'Tests no tests', nearly taken as evidence): squeezing the old form's budget to 1ms reproduces the exact production symptom, same AssertionError and 'Number of calls: 0', while the same old form at its normal budget under identical conditions passes; file runs 12/12 clean in isolation, so alone there is no load to blow the budget. Fixed with the act() drain pattern the sibling cases in the same file already carry and explain. Full suite 8/8 clean after, though at a 1-in-6 rate eight clean runs occur by luck about 23% of the time, so the mechanism is the load-bearing evidence, not the streak. Merged b826df5.

headline: Notes written outside the buzzer channel's range were being quietly changed to a different note, in the app and in the export alike. You are now told instead.
matters: If you wrote a bass note lower than the PSG buzzer channel can actually play, nothing complained: the app and the export both quietly moved it to the lowest note the driver has, so you would hear a wrong note in the right rhythm and have no reason to suspect anything. That is harder to notice than silence would be. The export now tells you which note and why. The same fix removes the opposite problem, where high notes the hardware CAN play were being refused for no reason. Separately, the app carries a copy of the driver's note table with a comment claiming it matches exactly, and nothing had ever checked that claim. It does match, all eighty four entries, and there is now a check that recomputes them from the driver's own source so it cannot drift unnoticed.
detail: SOUND-TRUTH row, both halves true for any driver list so neither waits on d-9. DEVIATION flagged: the brief said read from Memra's source; grounded against skdisasm instead because PSG_PERIOD_TABLE's comment claims it matches Flamedriver/S3K, Seraph's only registered profile is Flamedriver, and there is no Memra profile in this tree (F31 booked its absence), so checking an S3K table against Memra would manufacture drift rather than detect it. Memra source does exist (aeon/engine/sound, tools/gen_sound_tables.py) and is the right target once a Memra profile lands. Drift check: the driver stores frequencies in Hz, not periods, computing them at assembly time via min(3FFh, round(PSG_Sample_Rate/(f*2))) with PSG_Sample_Rate = Z80_Clock/16 and Z80_Clock = Master_Clock/15, so the test parses the Hz list and clock constants from the disassembly and applies the driver's own formula rather than comparing copy to copy. 84/84 exact today. Poisoned three ways: corrupting one entry names it (index 11: driver 0x388 vs table 0x389), unreachable source fails with instructions, deliberate opt-out skips; reuses F32's SERAPH_SKIP_ROM_TESTS so there is one knob. Range fix: validation used midi_to_smps_note (12-106) for every pitched channel but PSG's real range is 36-119 derived from the driver's table (z80 index 0-83, midi = index+36); wrong both ways, since 12-35 passed then got retuned by smps_note_name_psg's .max(0) clamp plus midi_to_psg_period's bottom entry, and 107-119 was refused though table and exporter both handle it. Framing corrected on evidence: these notes are retuned, not silenced. Four tests, two controls, poisoned by restoring the channel-agnostic check. Merged bebea01. Lanes: cargo 281 passed 0 failed, build exit 0 zero warnings, vitest 352/352, no bindings drift.

headline: A test that had been failing at random for reasons nobody had pinned down is now understood and fixed. It was the test clicking a button before the window had finished loading, not the app misbehaving.
matters: It was reporting the app as failing to create a project, which is the opposite of what was happening. A test that lies about which side is broken costs more than one that simply fails.
detail: F42. My diagnosis (a one second polling budget, as with this morning's flake) was REFUTED by the agent: handleCreate calls ipc.createProject synchronously before its first await, so the budget cannot decide it. Real cause: the helper clicked Create before the driver list effect had run, so the dialog refused with Select a driver and the poll waited for a call that could never come. Caught unforced on the ORIGINAL file under 48 spinners, failing at line 114. All 4 waitFor sites in the file converted; waitFor no longer imported. No product code touched.

headline: A test that randomly claimed copying a section did nothing is understood and fixed. The app was fine; the test was pressing the key before the app had finished listening for it.
matters: It failed about one run in three and only when the whole suite ran at once, which is the kind of failure that gets shrugged at until it hides a real one. It is now explained down to the mechanism rather than made to go away.

matters: The code that handles a finished import even says in its own comment that it is the same boundary as opening a project. The prompt exists, and one of the three doors onto it simply does not use it. Not fixed yet, because it was outside what that piece of work was allowed to change.

headline: The seven leftover copies of the project from finished work are deleted, on your word. That gave back 29 GB of disk.
